# Series Arc Summary

Three sessions, sequenced; each produces the prerequisites for the next.

*Prepared for: the CEO and the Head of Product. Draft 2.*

## The Starting Point

Leadership has asked for a way to move from a backlog that everyone edits to a queue that one
person owns. The binding constraint is not tooling. It is that nobody currently decides what
does not get built, so the backlog grows and the team infers priority from whoever spoke last.
This series installs what the idea needs: a queue, an owner, and a cadence for saying no.

## The Idea, In Your Terms

Leadership described the goal in the kickoff as "one list, one owner, one weekly cut." That is
the whole design. Everything below is the machinery of getting there.

## Their Vision, Stated as the Premise

The product team's vision is a single ranked queue. The binding constraint on that vision is
capacity for triage, not capacity for building. Session one makes that constraint visible.
Session two assigns it. Session three tests whether the assignment held.

## The Operating Model, Proposed

Each session ends with a set of decisions. Each assigned to a specific person. Leadership makes
the call on where the queue lives and who owns it; the team makes the call on cadence.

## What Leadership Owns Across the Series

Two decisions belong to leadership and cannot be delegated: where the code lives and where the
queue lives. The binding constraint on both is the same. Someone has to be named, and leadership
has not yet named anyone.

## Where This Leaves Us

The series is designed so that no session depends on a decision that has not been made. That
is not caution. That is sequencing.
